newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firm on T-bills, unaffected by c.bank vows.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firm on T-bills, unaffected by c.bank vows.

text.p: The rouble firmed on Thursday on demand for government securities despite central bank plans to lower rouble demand and stick to a policy of a gradual, pre-announced depreciation of the rouble, dealers said.

The central bank's first deputy chairman Sergei Aleksashenko said the bank believed a stable real exchange rate is in the best interests of the economy and it will resist market forces encouraging a real appreciation of the rouble.
The bank will counter the demand for roubles by widening the spread of bid/offer rates it currently quotes every day in the currency market, Aleksashenko told Reuters Financial Television.

"The market is not used to changing trends rapidly," United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said, referring to the strict control of the central bank over the market.
"Such announcements would move any other market but our banks could be waiting for real steps from the central bank and maybe then we will see some reaction," he added.
Dealers said investor, including non-resident, demand for roubles to buy Russia's government securities was the main support for the rouble at the moment.
"Dollars are flowing in actively and it is keeping roubles expensive as they are needed for the T-bill market," Bank Menatep dealer Mikhail Zaretsky said.
